mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Extract of Corporation Establishment Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Section, District Court of the Republic of Korea with territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Destination is an Apostille Convention Party: obtain an original or certified copy from the District Court Registry, then submit directly to the Apostille Section, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MOFA), for a single Hague Apostille. Destination is not an Apostille Convention Party: obtain the certified copy from the District Court Registry, obtain MOFA authentication of the court official's signature, then submit to the Consular Legalization Section of the destination-country Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certified Copy of the Entire Corporate Register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea having jurisdiction over the company's registered seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Destination is an Apostille Convention Party: issue/obtain the certified corporate register extract from the Registry, then apply to MOFA Apostille Section for a Hague Apostille. Destination is not an Apostille Convention Party: obtain the extract, have MOFA authenticate the court registrar's signature, then have the destination-country Embassy or Consulate in Seoul perform Consular Legalization. The two authentication pathways are exclusive alternatives and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Yuhan Hoesa Articles)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public authorized under the Korean Notary Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille Convention destination: after execution by all incorporators, have the Korean notary public notarize the signatures, then apply to MOFA for a Hague Apostille on the notary's signature and seal. For a non-Apostille destination: after notarization, obtain MOFA authentication, then present the document to the Consular Legalization Section of the destination-country Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive paths; use only the path applicable to the destination state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Appointing Initial Director and Representative and Granting Power of Attorney for Bank and Payment-Rail Onboarding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of KR_YUHANGHOESA (initial incorporators acting before registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Destination is an Apostille Convention Party: have the corporate representative sign the resolution in the presence of a Korean notary public, notarize the signature and seal, then apply to MOFA Apostille Section for a Hague Apostille. Destination is not an Apostille Convention Party: notarize the resolution, obtain MOFA authentication of the notary's signature, then deliver to the destination-country Embassy or Consulate in Seoul for Consular Legalization. The two paths are alternative, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Seal Impression (Certified Copy of Company Seal Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea where the company seal is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the seal certificate from the District Court Registry. For an Apostille Convention destination, submit the certificate to MOFA Apostille Section for a Hague Apostille. For a non-Apostille destination, obtain MOFA authentication of the court signature and then apply to the destination-country Embassy or Consulate in Seoul for Consular Legalization. Use only the single applicable path; do not chain apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank where the company will maintain its operating account and Stripe/PayPal settlement account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank officer must sign the reference letter and the bank corporate seal must be affixed. Destination is an Apostille Convention Party: have the bank officer's signature notarized by a Korean notary and apply to MOFA Apostille Section for a Hague Apostille. Destination is not an Apostille Convention Party: have the bank officer's signature notarized, obtain MOFA authentication, and then obtain Consular Legalization from the destination-country Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. Use one path only depending on the destination country.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, signatories, and beneficial owners at or above the 25% statutory threshold must be screened prior to execution of the formation block and continuously thereafter. Screening must cover the consolidated United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Korean FIU designations under the Specific Financial Information Act, the U.S. OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, the UK HMT Consolidated Sanctions List, and the EU Financial Sanctions Lists. Every potential match must be resolved through documented disposition and escalated to the AML compliance officer. Politically Exposed Persons, including family members and close associates, receive enhanced due diligence with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds analysis, senior management approval, and transaction monitoring. High-risk jurisdictions, nominee indicators, shell-company red flags, inconsistent beneficial ownership data, and unusual request patterns trigger additional verification. No payment rails such as Stripe or PayPal may be activated until beneficial ownership has been independently verified through reliable documents or electronic KYC evidence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea, National Court Administration, integrated with the Commercial Registration Information System; tax-registration name clearance is handled by the National Tax Service Hometax system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be written in the Korean alphabet (Hangul) as the statutory register name; a Latin-script English name may be used for international contracts and tax invoices only as an auxiliary transliteration of the registered Hangul name. The registrar applies a four-tier structural review: (1) distinctive element, (2) objective business-purpose phrase, (3) legal form designation 'Yuhan Hoesa' displaying limited liability, and (4) transliteration or foreign-language suffix where relevant. Transliteration must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean for consistency with international records. The name must not be identical or substantially misleadingly similar to an existing registered trade name or trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Holding (where banking approval would be required)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may first file a written objection with the same registration officer at the competent District Court registry, requesting reconsideration and correction of the stated grounds. The registrar must review the objection and either accept the name or issue a formal written rejection. If the formal rejection is upheld, the applicant may, within two weeks from receipt of the notice, file an immediate appeal to the district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, together with a certified copy of the rejection notice and supporting trade-name search evidence. In parallel, the applicant may withdraw the rejected application and file a fresh formation application with a new distinctive element. For tax-registration name rejections, a separate administrative appeal may be submitted to the National Tax Service through the local tax office. All appeal documents should be filed within the statutory time limits to preserve standing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a stock photography and generative visual assets Yuhan Hoesa engaged in cross-border digital-content sales, Korean commercial law requires a genuine registered office capable of receiving service of process and tax notices. A postal-mailbox or non-attended virtual office is rejected by the National Tax Service and by commercial banks because it raises shell-company and substance-shifting indicators. A permissible arrangement is a licensed serviced-office or business-center lease with a dedicated room, 24-hour mail handling, telephone line, boardroom access, and at least one authorized officer physically present on reasonable notice. Stripe and PayPal underwriting teams and Korean settlement banks generally require an actual lease contract, business license, and physical inspection; therefore, a 'virtual mailbox only' solution is not acceptable for this industry, while a fully serviced physical business suite is operationally and bankably acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspection checklist: registered office signage, lease or use-right contract, corporate seal and certificate, board minutes, incoming mail log, bank statements and settlement records, VAT invoices, employment contracts or outsource vendor agreements, computer/server or cloud-storage evidence of stock-photo and AI-asset operations, and availability of a responsible person. Quantified risk: approximately 8-12% in the first fiscal year where a serviced physical office is maintained; approximately 35-55% where a mail-only or unstaffed virtual office is used, due to mandatory irregular audits by the National Tax Service, local municipal tax inspectors, and bank account-compliance visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 543 through 613 (Limited Liability Company / Yuhan Hoesa), including formation, contribution, directorship, supervision and registration provisions; supplemented by the Registration of Real Estate and Corporation Act and the Corporate Registration Rules of the Supreme Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, operating under the Supreme Court Registration Bureau; online filings are accepted through the Internet Registration Office (IROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), together with notarized Articles of Incorporation, contribution payment certificates, and the consent forms of the initial directors and auditor.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The capital amount and member contribution schedule are set in the Articles of Incorporation. Each member's monetary contribution must be fully paid or contributed before the incorporation registration, and payment must be evidenced by a bank remittance receipt or bank certificate. There is no separate blocked escrow account requirement under the Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; any escrow arrangement is optional and would only be imposed by the bank or an existing financing agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], A KOREAN YUHAN HOESA LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, ADOPTED AT THE FIRST STATUTORY MEETING OF DIRECTORS. The undersigned, being all of the duly appointed and qualified directors of [Company Name] (the "Company"), a Yuhan Hoesa established under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, do hereby waive any further notice of the first meeting of directors and adopt the following resolutions by unanimous written consent in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Commercial Act. FIRST: RESOLVED, that the Company's initial subscribed capital as set forth in the notarized Articles of Incorporation is hereby ratified, acknowledged, and accepted. The directors confirm that each member's contribution has been fully paid or transferred as required by the Articles, and that evidence of contribution payment, including bank remittance receipts or certificates, has been or will be delivered to the competent District Court Registry as a condition of incorporation. SECOND: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be at [Full Address], Republic of Korea, and the directors are authorized to execute, notarize, and file the incorporation registration application, business registration application, and all related statutory forms necessary to establish the registered office and to bind the Company to all obligations arising from such office. THIRD: RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to select and open a principal operating account with a commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, to appoint authorized signatories, to execute account opening instruments, and to establish payment collection channels, including foreign currency settlements as needed for the Company's stock-photography and generative visual content marketplace. FOURTH: RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers be appointed: [Name], Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [Name], Director and Chief Operating Officer; and [Name], Director and Compliance Officer / Secretary. Each appointed officer is authorized, within the limits of the Articles and applicable law, to represent the Company, execute contracts, issue invoices, make regulatory filings, open and operate bank accounts, and supervise employees and service providers. FIFTH: RESOLVED, that the directors and officers are severally authorized to prepare, submit, and cure all documentation, to pay all appropriate fees and taxes, to engage counsel and notaries, and to do all other acts necessary to complete the Company's incorporation, corporate governance organization, and post-formation compliance. SIXTH: RESOLVED, that this resolution shall be effective immediately and a copy of these resolutions shall be placed with the Company's statutory records and filed with the relevant authorities where required. Drafted and adopted by unanimous written consent of the directors this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean notary public commissioned by the Ministry of Justice (the notarial office of the local Bar Association or a designated KORA-NOTA notary).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language and have each founding member or their lawful agent execute them. The notary must verify legal capacity, voluntary execution, and identity. The Articles must state the corporate purpose, trade name, registered office, capital amount, contribution method, member identities, officer arrangements, and public notice method. The notarized Articles are a statutory prerequisite for registration; any subsequent amendment before filing requires re-notarization or a notarial addendum. Foreign founders should provide passport copies and, if applicable, an apostilled or consularized power of attorney. The exact corporate name is checked on the Court Registry name search before notarization.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or national ID of each founding member
Power of attorney and apostille/consular certificate for foreign representatives, if any
Certificate of corporate seal or individual seal certificate, if available
Proof of corporate name reservation or name search result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requests corrections, amend the draft and resubmit. If identity verification is challenged, provide updated apostilled or legalized identification and proof of appointment. In case of notarial refusal, seek a second notary or apply to the court for a substitute notarial act under the Korean Notary Act, although re-filing is usually faster.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Contribution Payment and Bank Payment Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean commercial bank authorized by the Financial Services Commission, selected by the Company (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, Hana, or Nonghyup).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company formation account or use the designated account number stated in the Articles. Each member remits or transfers the full amount of his or her subscribed contribution to that account. The bank issues a certificate of contribution payment or transaction statement showing the contributor and amount. The Company must ensure that the aggregate amount matches the total capital stated in the Articles. For cross-border remittances from foreign members, the remittance reference must state the company name and articles number, and the bank may request beneficial ownership documentation for AML/KYC purposes. The payment certificate will be submitted to the District Court Registry together with the incorporation registration application.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation
Company pre-registration account opening form
Member identification and AML/KYC forms
Remittance slips or foreign exchange transaction certificates
Bank contribution payment certificate request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the payment due to AML concerns, supply source-of-funds evidence and an execution structure chart. If the remittance lacks the company reference, ask the remitting bank to issue a correction or provide a declaration from the sender. If the aggregate payment is short, either collect the difference or amend the Articles to reduce the stated capital before re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court in the jurisdiction of the registered office; online via Internet Registration Office (IROS) at iros.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the statutory incorporation registration application with the court registry within the period specified by the Commercial Act. The application must attach the notarized Articles, the contribution payment certificate, the consent or appointment forms for the initial directors and statutory administrator(s), and proof that registration tax and education surtax were paid. The court will review the corporate name, purpose, capital, contribution, and governance structure. Upon approval, the court enters the Company in the Commercial Registry and issues a Certificate of Corporate Registration. The Company is legally formed as of that registration. Registration tax is assessed ad valorem on subscribed capital and paid by revenue stamp or account transfer.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation (court form)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of contribution payment from the bank
Consent forms of the first directors and auditor
Certificate of payment of registration tax and education surtax
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if any
Lease agreement or landlord consent for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementation order (bonyeong), correct the identified deficiencies within the stated cure period, typically not exceeding two weeks, or file a written explanation. If registration is refused, submit an immediate appeal (a complaint) to the competent appellate court within two weeks. The agent should also re-verify the corporate name, the notarization, and bank certificate validity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (Jeseo-seo) under the National Tax Service; online via HomeTax at hometax.go.kr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration has been completed, file the corporate business registration application with the tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office. This must be done within the statutory period from the date of incorporation. Submit the Certificate of Corporate Registration, a lease contract or landlord consent, the representative director's identification, and the corporate seal certificate. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate (Sa-up-ja-deung-deung-jeung) and classify the company for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and wage withholding. The company must also determine whether a downtown branch, online marketplace, or merchandising activity registration is required; however, for a pure digital stock-photography platform no industrial operating license is required.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate business registration
Certificate of Corporate Registration from the court
Lease agreement or rent receipt and landlord consent
Copy of representative director's passport or ID
Corporate seal certificate
First board resolution authorizing the business registration filing
Bank account payment evidence for fees if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the place of business, submit an amended lease, a rent deposit payment receipt, or a usage recognition letter from the owner. If the representative is unavailable, provide a power of attorney with the seal certificate. If the business purpose is flagged for licensing, provide the certification of exemption or the relevant IT/telecom registration, but no manufacturing permit is applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Governance, Bank Account Activation and Compliance File Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and statutory officers of the Company; external banks; HomeTax and the Court Registry for subsequent filings; Korean Financial Intelligence Unit for AML notifications if applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first statutory meeting of directors to adopt the first board resolution and approve the governance file. Open permanent operating bank accounts and supply the court registration and business registration certificates to the bank. Register the corporate seal card, issue the corporate seal certificate, and appoint the bank signatories. Register an email account with HomeTax for e-tax invoices, apply for the corporate digital certificate, and set up the stock-photography marketplace payment rails through Stripe and PayPal in line with the bank's foreign currency guidelines. Maintain statutory records: articles of incorporation, member register, register of directors, minutes, contribution receipts, and copies of all licenses. If any officer changes occur after incorporation, file the director changes with the court registry and tax office within their prescribed deadlines.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written consent of the first board meeting
Certificate of Corporate Registration and Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal registration certificate
Account opening forms and AML/KYC documents for signatories
Schedule of beneficial owners and member register
HomeTax sign-up forms and email registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank rejects an account application due to compliance risk, submit a board resolution identifying the economic purpose, a UBO schedule, and projected transaction flows, or apply to a second-tier bank; if the tax office rejects e-tax invoice registration, correct the email verification and corporate digital certificate within the appeal period. Update the registry promptly if the registered office or representatives change.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the ISIC 7420 commercial stock photography and generative visual assets activity is a pure digital/consulting service with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit is mandated for a pure digital stock-photography marketplace under Korean national or municipal licensing maps.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical establishment; the Korean Ministry of Environment and regional environmental agencies have no permitting footprint for this digital activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - exempt from the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and the rules on environmental impact statements because the activity generates no construction, land alteration, or physical installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the activity produces no wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or stack emissions; only ordinary office utility consumption and electronic equipment disposal, which is covered by local municipal waste rules if the Company uses a standard office lease.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit or hazardous occupancy clearance is required. If the Company leases a standard office, the landlord is responsible for the fundamental fire-fighting installations under the Firefighting Facilities Installation and Safety Control Act, and the Company shall simply maintain a safe workplace and standard insurance in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with online electronic operations administered through the HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr) and the NTS Information Trading System (EDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is a resident domestic corporation and must apply for a Business Operator Registration Number at the district tax office having jurisdiction over its registered head office or domestic place of business. The application is submitted through HomeTax or to the competent head tax office using the statutory Business Registration application, attaching the articles of incorporation, certificate of corporate seal registration, certificate of incorporation or foreign business registration of non-resident shareholders where relevant, identity documents of directors, and evidence of the principal place of business. For a non-resident foreign entity that is not locally incorporated but is engaged in Korean VAT-taxable supplies, the foreign entity must appoint a domestic tax representative and file the same Business Registration application in the name of the foreign business operator through the NTS HomeTax portal. The NTS typically issues the Business Operator Registration Number within 3 to 5 business days, and that registration number simultaneously becomes the VAT registration identifier and the corporate income tax identifier. Passive non-resident shareholders of a Korean Yuhan Hoesa are not required to obtain a separate Korean VAT ID solely for their shareholding; the corporate entity holds the Korean TIN/VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election or an S-corporation-style election for a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company. A Korean domestic corporation is mandatorily taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and VAT registration is compulsory; there is no pass-through election for stock photography licensing income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold applies to a Korean-incorporated Yuhan Hoesa; it must obtain VAT registration and issue tax invoices from business commencement regardless of revenue. The KRW 80,000,000 simplified-taxpayer annual turnover ceiling is available only to individual entrepreneurs and therefore cannot be used by the corporate Yuhan Hoesa. Foreign non-resident suppliers of digital services to Korean consumers are also subject to VAT registration without any turnover exemption threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices for taxable supplies and transmit them to the NTS through HomeTax or NTS-approved EDI software by the day following supply. The NTS operates a real-time electronic tax invoice collection system; there is no third-party fiscal clearance stamping machine for VAT in Korea, but the e-tax invoice must carry a sequential supply number, supplier VAT ID, recipient VAT ID, supply value, VAT amount, and zero-rated export indicator where applicable. Failure to transmit a valid electronic tax invoice or intentional issuance of a false export invoice triggers statutory penalties and may invalidate the buyer's input VAT claim.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The Yuhan Hoesa may claim 0% VAT on the supply of stock photography and AI-generated visual asset licenses to customers located outside the Republic of Korea, provided the services are supplied to and actually used by the non-resident customer outside Korea, are paid in foreign currency or otherwise as contractually agreed, and are properly evidenced as export service transactions. Physical export of a server or digital medium is not required; the critical statutory condition is that the benefit or legal license is entirely obtained outside South Korea by a non-resident party. Zero-rating is also available for supplies of goods physically shipped outside Korea after customs export formalities are completed. All zero-rated export supplies must be reported on the VAT return and accompanied by supporting documentation retained by the taxpayer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration approved by Korea Customs Service, or the electronic export declaration number for physical goods exported from Korea
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport document evidencing physical movement of goods out of Korea (for goods exports only)
Commercial invoice describing the licensed digital content, license term, territory, price, and explicit indication that the supply is exported or supplied to a non-resident customer
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued through HomeTax or NTS-approved EDI showing the supply as tax-exempt export zero-rated transaction
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or inward remittance certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank demonstrating receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Executed license agreement or stock media purchase order demonstrating that the end customer is a non-resident and the license is for use outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may open an export zero-rating audit and apply the standard five-year statute of limitations; if export documentation is missing, fraudulent, or inconsistent, the NTS will claw back the zero-rated treatment, reassess VAT at 10%, and impose statutory additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes. Negligent under-reporting generally attracts an additional tax of 10% of the unpaid tax amount, fraudulent under-reporting attracts 20% to 40%, and knowingly fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating may also trigger the criminal penalty provisions of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. Late-payment interest accrues on all reassessed VAT, and fictitious export tax invoices may trigger separate tax invoice penalties as well as refusal/denial of export refunds. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day foreign exchange settlement deadline for export-related transactions, without an approved extension, may additionally constitute a violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and result in fines and further administrative sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Federation of Banks' Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) registered as the delegated foreign exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is freely convertible for current account transactions, while capital account transactions are subject to registration, declaration, or licensing under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. A foreign-invested stock photo marketplace operating as a Yuhan Hoesa may convert inbound paid-in capital to KRW after the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) report is filed with a designated foreign exchange bank; profit remittance in the form of dividends is regarded as a current account payment and may be remitted after the tax withholdings and the legal requirements of the Foreign Exchange Information System are satisfied. No mandatory percentage of realized foreign currency revenue must be exchanged into KRW; however, 100 percent of export proceeds must be repatriated through an authorized bank in Korea within the legally stipulated time limit, and any retention in an overseas account requires a separate overseas current account permit. For digital content and royalty income, the remittance of service proceeds requires a service contract, foreign currency invoice, and prescribed transaction report to the designated bank in advance. In practice, KRW convertibility is high for onshore licensed banks, but non-residents are not able to maintain free offshore KRW accounts, and settlement of domestic expenses creates a forced KRW conversion.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds for digital content and services must be collected within 6 months from the date of service provision unless an extension is granted, while goods exports enjoy an 18-month collection period. The statutory surrender requirement is effectively 100 percent repatriation to a domestic foreign exchange account or settlement to an authorized foreign exchange bank, but the mandatory conversion ratio into KRW is 0 percent for proceeds held in a permitted foreign currency account. Proceeds must be reported via the Foreign Exchange Information System within the bank's reporting calendar; a separately approved overseas current account is needed if funding is to remain offshore.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational KRW Account with integrated FEIS reporting

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMI accounts are not viable as primary banking rails for a Korean LLC. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires resident legal entities to carry out foreign exchange transactions with licensed foreign exchange banks, and foreign EMIs such as Wise or Revolut are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission (FSC) to provide Korean corporate accounts, local currency settlement, tax invoice support, or capital receipts verification. They may be used only as marginal collection aggregators for customer card payments, but the account must be funded and swept to a Tier-1 bank account, and any payment gateway must operate in compliance with the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Overall feasibility for treasury purposes is Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Domestic Tier-1 Korean banks require physical presence for the initial corporate account opening interview of the representative director and any natural person UBO. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted as a complete substitute; a board-authorized local director or locally present shareholder may attend the branch with original corporate documentation. For non-resident directors, Korean banks may request either a physical visit or a video interview accepted under their internal CDD policy, but foreign documents require apostilled extracts and either a notarized original passport signature or bank-issued consular confirmation. In all cases at least one authorised signatory with a Korean residence registration number or Alien Registration Card is needed for practical operational continuity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual or offshore holding company identified as ultimate beneficial owner, creating opacity around fund origin and transfer chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited shareholder profile, passport notarized by a notary public and apostilled, certified corporate registry extract for any intermediary entities, beneficial ownership declaration naming all beneficial owners above 10 percent, banking references not older than 3 months, and the latest audited financial statements or tax returns of each shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue model is a marketplace with many low-level micro-payments from Stripe or PayPal, presenting inconsistent invoice evidence and third-party payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed Stripe and PayPal platform service agreements, merchant ID registration certificate, deterministic revenue flow diagram from platform to settlement bank, export VAT or withholding invoices for the last 6 months, a sample set of customer licensing contracts with digital signature logs, and a written revenue assurance questionnaire completed by the CFO or external accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign capital injection into a Korean LLC is pending FIPA report; banks may flag potential violation of FDI declaration timing if funds are received before the report is filed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-landing receipt of the Foreign Investment Declaration report stamped by the designated bank, remittance instruction letter with purpose code 'Foreign direct investment in Korean company', bank telegraphic transfer acknowledgment, source of funds documentation such as three-month personal bank statements or corporate financial statements, and the signed foreign-invested enterprise articles of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sensitive IP and AI-generated content trading may trigger sanctions or PEP screening because counterparties are online and not vetted.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions screening logs, country exclusion policy for all marketplace customers, IP content moderation compliance certificates, proof of registration of the entity at its registered Korean address, lease or title deed of registered office, and a sworn declaration that transactions will not involve politically exposed persons or sanctioned jurisdictions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must submit a Foreign Investment Declaration under FIPA to a designated foreign exchange bank before remitting equity capital. The injection must then be executed with a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own bank account, with remittance purpose code 'Foreign direct investment in Korean company' under FEIS rules and the overseas remitter exactly matching the declared foreign investor. The designated bank must issue a capital verification certificate upon presentation of the inward remittance advice, the declared FDI amount certificate, and the bank's passbook entry. The funds are lodged in a foreign investment proceeds account at a Tier-1 domestic bank, and conversion to KRW is executed only after the bank confirms the FIPA report is complete; no working capital may be disbursed before capital verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For royalty payments to foreign contributors, use SWIFT MT103 with source country and purpose code 'Royalties for intellectual property license' after exact withholding tax reconciliation under the applicable Korea tax treaty. For stock photo distribution agreements, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not necessary and are used only in exceptional physical-media bulk orders; the standard rail is direct wire transfer against a pro-forma or commercial invoice with the underlying stock photo or non-exclusive license agreement. All outbound payments require prior FEIS report if exceeding the statutory equivalent threshold, and the bank must receive a standard foreign exchange contract form, contract copy, tax invoice, and evidence of withholding tax payment before processing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts with licensed banks for documented trade or service receivables denominated in USD, EUR, or JPY up to the expected contractual exposure
Cross-currency swaps between KRW and USD for managed reinvestment of retained foreign earnings, subject to FEIS reporting and underlying exposure validation
Onshore FX swaps to cover short-term mismatch between the timing of export proceeds receipts and KRW operational disbursements

Offshore non-deliverable forwards are generally not available to onshore Korean residents and should not form the treasury framework; any hedging must be settled through a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and statutory retention of approved financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Act corporate governance record retained at the registered office; no separate government filing required unless articles are amended and a certified copy must be filed with the Local Court Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end; for a 31 December year end, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting or to prepare and retain the financial statements may expose the managing member to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act; habitual failure to maintain corporate records can be treated as evidence of dormancy and, combined with years of unfiled tax returns, may lead to administrative strike-off of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return with financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the year immediately following a 31 December fiscal year end; within 3 months after the close of a non-calendar fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a negligence addition under the Framework Act on National Taxes of up to 20% of the underpaid corporate tax for under-reporting, 40% for fraudulent non-filing, and daily overdue interest at approximately 0.022%; persistent failure to file for multiple consecutive years can trigger estimated assessment, asset seizure, and ultimately administrative strike-off by the registry on the prosecutor's request.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax preliminary and final periodic returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half: preliminary return due 25 April, final return due 25 July; second half: preliminary return due 25 October, final return due 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing adds 10% of the unpaid output VAT as a late-filing surcharge plus daily overdue interest of approximately 0.022%; repeated failure to file VAT returns on a digital stock-media platform may result in VAT deregistration, tax collection seizure, and for a dormant entity, administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified auditor's report and audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and, if the company is a public issuer or otherwise covered by disclosure obligations, the Financial Supervisory Service through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System; audited financial statements are also attached to the corporate income tax return filed with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor's report must be presented to members before the annual general meeting, which must be held within 6 months after fiscal year end; the tax filing deadline is 31 March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company above the mandatory audit threshold that fails to appoint a certified CPA auditor is subject to a correction order and administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; non-audited financial statements can be rejected for corporate tax purposes, and persistent non-compliance combined with annual filing omissions can expose the entity to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll withholding settlement and wage and tax statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 10 March of the year following the calendar year in which wages were paid, where the Yuhan Hoesa has employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission of withholding statements attracts withholding negligence additions and daily overdue interest on unpaid withheld income tax; continued failure may make the managing member personally liable and block issuance of tax clearance certificates, contributing to a dormant-entity strike-off if the registered office remains inactive.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa with corporate status is legally required to undergo an independent certified CPA audit if it meets any one of the following quantitative triggers at fiscal year end: (1) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion; (2) annual revenue equals or exceeds KRW 70 billion; (3) average number of full-time employees equals or exceeds 300; or (4) the company is listed or required to file with the Financial Supervisory Service. In addition, an entity with total assets between KRW 7 billion and KRW 12 billion becomes subject to audit if it simultaneously exceeds KRW 30 billion of annual revenue and 200 full-time employees. These thresholds are converted at the prevailing Bank of Korea exchange rate for US dollar financial reporting purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) applies to externally audited and listed entities; private small- and medium-sized Yuhan Hoesa entities that are not subject to mandatory external audit may apply K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) as permitted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. Revenue from stock-photo licensing and generative visual assets must be recognized under the revenue standard equivalent to IFRS 15.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A private Korean Yuhan Hoesa does not file a separate annual UBO declaration form, but the register of members must be reviewed annually and the current controlling member status must be reflected in the corporate income tax return and shareholding disclosures. Any transfer of membership interests must be reported to the managing member and entered in the register of members within 30 days, and the prior member must be identified in the attending members' resolution minute. If any individual member holds 5% or more, that beneficial ownership is confirmed annually in the statutory register review and, where applicable, in filings required by financial or competent authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Members' Meetings and Board Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,800 per annum for a compliant registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 per annum for a low-risk stock-media platform with mid-volume cross-border payment activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: South Korea applies progressive corporate tax rates: 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 20% on income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion, and 25% on income exceeding KRW 20 billion. Applicable incentives for a digital stock photography and generative visual assets entity include the R&D tax credit for software and AI-related development expenses, the Tax Credit for Job Creation, and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax incentives including a 50% corporate tax reduction for up to 5 years for qualifying foreign-invested high-tech businesses in free economic zones. No general patent box regime exists; however, the IP income exclusion under the Corporate Tax Law applies to qualifying acquired or developed patented technologies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: South Korea Corporate Tax Return, Form 1 (法人세과세표준및세액계산서) filed via the HomeTax System (홈택스) for domestic corporations and the National Tax Service's electronic filing portal; foreign corporations use the corresponding alien corporation return form.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year (Article 60, Corporate Tax Act). For a December year-end, the deadline is March 31. For non-resident corporations, the deadline is also 3 months after year-end, but where the foreign corporation is subject to domestic place of effective management rules, the deadline may be aligned with the Korean fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification details: registered corporate name, business registration number (사업자등록번호), tax office code, fiscal year start and end dates, and resident representative legal personality details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Yuhan Hoesa stock photography AI entity, enter the exact legal name as registered with the Korean court registry, the 10-digit business registration number, and the fiscal year. Non-resident shareholders need not appear in this box unless the entity is a foreign-invested company subject to Foreign Investment Notification under Article 5 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; if so, the foreign investment report number should be added in the remarks column.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue recognition summary: gross sales, service revenue, digital content revenue, royalty income, and other operating income derived from stock photography licensing, AI-generated visual asset subscriptions, and ancillary API access fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue from Korean customers must be fully accrued regardless of whether collection occurs through Stripe or PayPal. Cross-border digital sales to foreign consumers may be treated as foreign source income if the place of supply is outside Korea, but ensure the place of effective management is not triggered by server location alone. For intercompany licensing of AI model output to related offshore affiliates, apply the arm's length principle under Article 5 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs; do not omit deemed royalty income from related-party data usage agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct production costs: server hosting, cloud computing, AI training data licensing, freelance photographer commissions, API integration costs, and direct costs attributable to creating and hosting digital stock images.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct apportioned hosting and cloud costs to the extent incurred for producing locally taxable revenue. Payments to non-resident photographers are subject to withholding tax under the Corporate Tax Act Article 98 and the Personal Income Tax Act Article 156; if the recipient is in a DTA jurisdiction, apply treaty withholding if the services do not constitute a permanent establishment. For AI model training data sourced overseas, ensure that any contingent royalty or license payment is documented with valid transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit calculation in relation to trading income: Box 2 less Box 3, aligned with the tax accounting treatment of a digital content enterprise.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For stock photography marketplaces, the gross profit margin must be compared with internal comparables of uncontrolled digital marketplace operators. If the Korean entity is classified as a limited-risk distributor or marketing and sales service provider, the transfer pricing adjustment could increase taxable profit; hence, maintain a functional and risk analysis to support the reported gross margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general, and administrative expenses: employee wages, marketing and platform user acquisition, legal and accounting fees, software development, depreciation of fixed assets, and insurance premiums.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean statutory document requirements apply: all expenses must be supported by bona fide tax invoices (세금계산서) in order to be deductible. Credit card merchant fees paid to Korean payments providers are deductible. For related-party management fees and technical service fees paid offshore, strictly comply with the arm's length standard and report the details on the transfer pricing disclosure form with the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and tax adjustments: provision for bad debts, entertainment expenses, donations, depreciation differences, penalties, net operating loss carryforward utilization, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident related parties must be scrutinized; if a payment lacks economic substance, the Korean tax authority may recharacterize it as a constructive dividend. Donations deducted must not exceed statutory thresholds. For stock photo AI development, software-related research expenses should be separately schedule to claim the R&D tax credit. Cross-border payments to low-tax jurisdictions must be listed in the Country-by-Country reporting schedule if the group meets the KRW thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the underpaid tax if the underpayment exceeds the statutory threshold; a negligent or willful understatement penalty of 10% or 30% respectively applies; if the return is not filed within 6 months, the unfiled tax penalty increases to 20% of the unpaid tax, plus an interest surcharge of 1.2% per month from the original due date. For tax fraud or intentional omission with intent to evade, Article 12 of the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act provides for imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million. Failure to produce transfer pricing documentation may result in a penalty of up to KRW 100 million and denial of corresponding adjustments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) imposed on dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders under Articles 98 and 156 of the Corporate Tax Act and Personal Income Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced dividend withholding tax under the Korea–US, Korea–UK, or other DTA, the non-resident shareholder must submit a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the competent tax authority of the residence country, together with Form 16 (Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction) to the Korean withholding agent before or at the time of the dividend distribution. The beneficial ownership declaration must establish that the recipient is the actual owner of the dividend and not an agent, nominee, or conduit. If the DTA rate is 10% or 15%, the difference must be refunded through an amended return of the foreign corporation or withholding agent. The application deadline is by the last day of the fiscal year following the withholding event; failure to submit TRC results in application of the domestic 22% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties and interest paid to non-residents are subject to statutory withholding at 22% (20% plus 2% local income tax). Korea-US DTA reduces royalty withholding to 15% generally, and 10% for industrial/commercial royalties under certain conditions; interest is taxed at 10% in the source state under treaty; Korea-UK DTA provides 10% royalty and 10% interest rates generally; other treaties vary. To apply the reduced rate, the beneficial owner must provide a TRC and complete Form 16; royalties sourced in Korea are those paid for the use or right to use intangible property in Korea, including AI-generated visual asset licenses and database access fees.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, intercompany transactions with related parties exceeding KRW 10 billion per relevant year trigger the mandatory submission of Local File and Master File. The threshold is KRW 10 billion for the aggregate intercompany transaction amount. Small and medium enterprises are not automatically exempted if transactions exceed the threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 2-2 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The Korean entity must demonstrate sufficient economic substance through personnel, offices, decision-making functions, and risk-bearing capacity. For stock photography and AI visual asset business, Core Income-Generating Activities include AI algorithm research and development, content curation and quality control, platform server management, licensing contract negotiation, and assumption of content infringement liability. Where a Korean resident entity is treated as a foreign corporation's permanent establishment, domestic Korean income attribution must follow the Authorized OECD Approach. The Korean tax authorities may disregard a Korea-based paper LLC with no CIGA and reattribute income to the beneficial owner under the substance-over-form, resulting in personal and corporate penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Tax Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting revenue from stock photo licensing and AI-generated image sales, fabricating deductible expenses, or submitting false invoices to the National Tax Service to reduce Korean corporation tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act imposes imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 100 million; additionally, up to 3 years' imprisonment for failure to comply with tax payment duties under Article 4 of the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act; the National Tax Basic Act imposes a 40% penalty for fraudulent underreporting and 20% for negligent underreporting plus daily overdue interest of 1.2% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 8 of the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act, directors are personally liable when the corporation's tax offense is committed with the director's knowledge and negligence; courts may pierce the corporate veil under Article 2 of the Commercial Act if the company is a sham or its separate legal personality is abused. Directors face civil tort liability for the full amount of evaded taxes, a travel ban and blacklisting by the Ministry of Justice, a ban from serving as a registered director of any Korean company, and up to 5 years' imprisonment; restitution of evaded taxes and fines may be enforced through attachment of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Artificial Interposition for Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing the Korean Yuhan Hoesa with no staff, no physical office, no substantive decision-making, and routing overseas royalty or dividend income through a conduit jurisdiction merely to obtain treaty withholding benefits or to avoid Korean source tax, without performing any Core Income-Generating Activities such as AI content validation, marketing, or contract administration in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 2-2 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs and Article 5 of the Corporate Tax Act deny treaty benefits and recharacterize the structure; withholding tax is reassessed at the domestic 22% rate on the full outbound flows, and penalty interest applies. If the interposed entity is deemed a sham, tax adjustment notices are issued to the beneficial shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign tax returns for a shell company may be jointly and severally liable for the reassessed corporate income tax under Article 3(1) of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Civil liability includes restitution of the entire tax shortfall, interest, and penalties; criminal exposure arises under Article 16 of the Punishment of Tax Crimes Act for aiding tax evasion, leading to imprisonment up to 3 years. A director may also be named on the National Tax Service's serious violator blacklist with publication of personal information and restrictions on foreign travel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Failure in Cross-Border Payment Railing (Stripe/PayPal) and Suspicious Transaction Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The stock photo platform collects user payments through Stripe and PayPal but deliberately fails to verify beneficial owners of high-volume business accounts, processes refunds to non-contractual third parties, or fails to file suspicious transaction reports when unusual offshore payments from sanctioned jurisdictions are received, while simultaneously using the funds to pay phantom royalties to related companies in no-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 49 of the Financial Transaction Reports Act, failure to report a suspicious transaction is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million; the Financial Intelligence Unit may impose administrative sanctions, revoke the money-exchange business registration, and levy fines up to KRW 100 million under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. The Korean tax authorities may also adjust the unreported payment transactions as undisclosed gross income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately fail to report suspicious transactions face criminal prosecution under the Financial Transaction Reports Act; personal imprisonment of up to 5 years is possible. Directors may be held civilly liable for losses arising from laundering proceeds; the corporate veil will be pierced where the company was operated as a tool for illicit foreign payment flows, allowing courts to order personal forfeiture of assets equal to the laundered amount. Travel bans are routinely imposed during the criminal investigation.
